question: What is the main goal when a surgeon chooses the level for an amputation?

options.A: To completely eliminate all post-surgery pain
options.B: To shorten the duration of the surgical operation
options.C: To preserve maximum length and joint function
options.D: To prevent the need for any future wound dressings

explanation: Surgeons carefully choose the amputation level to save as much of the limb and joint as possible, which helps the patient use a prosthesis much easier later. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h1)

question: Why is a below-knee amputation usually preferred over an above-knee amputation when possible?

options.A: It requires a much shorter hospital stay for the patient
options.B: It preserves the knee joint for better walking energy efficiency
options.C: It eliminates the risk of developing a stump contracture
options.D: It completely stops the occurrence of phantom limb sensations

explanation: Keeping the knee joint intact requires far less physical energy when walking with an artificial leg compared to walking without a natural knee joint. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is a major benefit of having an amputee peer visitor talk to a patient before surgery?

options.A: It replaces the need for formal medical informed consent
options.B: It provides realistic reassurance and reduces anxiety
options.C: It completely stops phantom limb pain before it starts
options.D: It teaches the patient how to clean the surgical wound

explanation: Speaking with someone who has walked the same path helps patients visualize a hopeful future and eases their immediate fears about the surgery. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for a left leg amputation looks terrified and refuses to speak. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Tell the patient that worrying will only make recovery harder
options.B: Call the surgeon to cancel the operation right away
options.C: Sit quietly with the patient and offer a listening ear
options.D: Insist that the patient signs the consent form immediately

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space allows the patient to express overwhelming emotions and builds trust with the nursing team. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h2)

question: What critical safety item must be kept right at the bedside immediately after an amputation surgery?

options.A: A complete set of replacement prostheses
options.C: A sterile set of major surgical instruments
options.D: A tourniquet for emergency hemorrhage control

explanation: Because major blood vessels are cut during surgery, sudden severe bleeding is a life-threatening emergency that requires an immediate tourniquet at the bedside. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why do nurses use a pen to circle blood spots on a fresh post-operative stump dressing?

options.A: To mark the exact location where the surgeon needs to place stitches
options.B: To show the patient where the wound pain is coming from
options.C: To monitor how fast and how much the bleeding is spreading
options.D: To prevent the sterile bandage from falling apart prematurely

explanation: Drawing a line around drainage and noting the time provides a clear visual reference to see if bleeding is slowing down or actively worsening. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h3)

question: How is a phantom limb sensation different from phantom limb pain?

options.A: Phantom sensation requires emergency surgery, while phantom pain goes away without any treatment
options.B: Phantom sensation is caused by an infection, whereas phantom pain is caused by poor dressings
options.C: Phantom sensation is typically painless, whereas phantom pain involves burning or shooting aches
options.D: Phantom sensation only occurs in upper limbs, while phantom pain occurs only in lower limbs

explanation: Feeling that the missing limb is still there is a normal, painless neurological experience, whereas actual pain requires targeted medical management. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h4)

question: A patient cries out with severe burning pain in a foot that was surgically removed yesterday. How should the nurse view this?

options.A: As proof that the incorrect surgical site was operated on
options.B: As evidence that the surgical wound has completely broken open
options.C: As a sign that the patient is experiencing a severe psychiatric delusion
options.D: As genuine neuropathic pain requiring proper evaluation and treatment

explanation: Phantom limb pain is real physical pain driven by the nervous system, and nurses must validate the patient's experience rather than dismiss it. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which resting position helps prevent hip tightness in a patient with a below-knee amputation?

options.A: Sitting upright in a chair with knees bent
options.B: Lying flat on the stomach for short periods
options.C: Sleeping exclusively on the unoperated side
options.D: Propping the stump high up on a large pillow

explanation: Prone positioning stretches the hip muscles and counteracts the tendency of the joint to freeze in a bent position. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h5)

question: A nurse sees a pillow placed directly under an above-knee amputation stump to keep it elevated. What is the correct action?

options.A: Remove the pillow to prevent the development of a hip contracture
options.B: Add a second pillow underneath to ensure total comfort
options.C: Leave the pillow in place because it improves blood circulation
options.D: Instruct the patient to keep the stump in that exact position all day

explanation: Keeping the stump elevated on a pillow for too long causes the joint to stiffen in a flexed position, making future prosthetic walking difficult. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of applying an elastic bandage or shrinker sock to a healing stump?

options.A: To replace the need for physical therapy and muscle strengthening
options.B: To keep the skin warm in cold weather environments
options.C: To completely eliminate all chances of a wound infection developing
options.D: To shape the residual limb into a conical form for prosthetic fitting

explanation: Compression wrapping helps shrink and shape the stump into the tapered contour required to fit snugly inside an artificial limb socket. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why is upper body strength training important for patients who have had a lower limb amputation?

options.A: They will rely heavily on their arms to use assistive devices like crutches
options.B: Upper body muscles directly control the movement of the knee joint
options.C: Arm exercises improve blood circulation specifically to the remaining stump
options.D: Strong arms prevent the occurrence of phantom limb pain sensations

explanation: Patients use walking frames, crutches, and parallel bars extensively during early rehabilitation, requiring strong arm and shoulder muscles. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which emotional response is common in patients adjusting to a sudden limb amputation?

options.A: Stages of grief similar to the mourning process
options.B: Immediate and permanent excitement for new technology
options.C: Total memory loss regarding the surgical procedure
options.D: Complete emotional indifference toward physical changes

explanation: Losing a body part represents a major life loss, and patients naturally cycle through grief emotions like anger, sadness, and acceptance. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h7)

question: A patient who lost a leg three weeks ago refuses to look at the stump and pushes family away. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A physical infection developing deep inside the surgical wound
options.B: Severe physical exhaustion from lack of nighttime sleep
options.C: Difficulty with body image adaptation and emotional grief
options.D: An allergic reaction to the prescribed pain medications

explanation: Refusing to look at the residual limb and pushing loved ones away are classic signs of struggling to accept an altered body image. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h7)
